scenarios.label: Base case
scenarios.summary: Our documented default assumptions. Cash only: fuel savings minus electricity and the cost of pipes and equipment.

scenarios.label: Most realistic (our pick)
scenarios.summary: Base case plus two realism fixes: building thermal mass smooths the coldest-hour peaks, and the Fulton buildings Con Ed's pilot will serve are not claimed twice.
changes: Don't claim Con Ed pilot buildings: off → on

scenarios.label: Benefit the community
scenarios.summary: Counts the climate benefit at New York State's value of carbon ($212/t) and gives public housing and schools twice the weight when choosing who to connect.

scenarios.label: Most profit for the data-center owner
scenarios.summary: The data-center owner pays for everything and sells heat 10 % cheaper than each building pays today. Only connections that make the owner money are built.
changes: Whose money is maximised: everyone combined → data-center owner

scenarios.label: Biggest CO₂ cut
scenarios.summary: Puts a high price on carbon ($400/t) so the network reaches gas-heated buildings too, as long as the cut is real.

scenarios.label: If the data center switches to liquid cooling
scenarios.summary: Liquid-cooled servers return water at about 45 °C instead of 30 °C, so the heat pump works far less hard (COP about 4.6 instead of 3.1), and more of the servers' heat can be captured (10 MW of the building's ~16.5 MW average electricity use, vs 5 MW today). Gas-heated buildings start to pay off.

scenarios.label: Best case
scenarios.summary: The base-case network, tested with every uncertain input at the favourable end of its documented range.
changes: Network fixed to the base-case design (same buildings and pipes)

scenarios.label: Worst case
scenarios.summary: The base-case network, tested with every uncertain input at the unfavourable end of its range at once: costly pipes and power, cheap steam, a weaker heat pump, 500 h of outages in the coldest weeks, no LL97 credit. A bound, not a forecast.
changes: Network fixed to the base-case design (same buildings and pipes)
